Q116277737.summary: Set into the leather cover of a later Gospel lectionary, this ivory plaque shows Christ enthroned in a mandorla at the centre, while the four evangelists sit writing their Gospels in the corners, each inspired by his symbol. The Met notes charming details: Luke's ox seems literally to open his eyes, and Mark's lion appears to speak to him. The plaque thus presents Christ in Majesty as the living source of the four Gospels.
facts: The plaque probably once adorned an Ottonian Gospel book and now decorates a late-15th-century Gospel lectionary.
The volume belonged to Carl Wilhelm Zeisberg of Wernigerode and then the princely Stolberg library at Wernigerode before reaching George and Florence Blumenthal, who gave it to the Met in 1941.
The Met dates the plaque 1000–1100 and places it in Cologne.
Q116277737.notes: Met 41.100.168. The Met's medium describes the whole volume (parchment manuscript with leather binding); the depiction is the ivory plaque.
